questions.prompt: Jordan catches himself starting with a Red line at the coat check after one guest misses a sign. Which response fits the ladder best?
choices: Red-first certainty would keep the sharp warning so the guest remembers next time.
Green-first clarity would restate the coat limit once and offer the umbrella stand.
Overexplaining safety would add several reasons before Jordan names the actual limit.

questions.prompt: A clinic log shows 3 drafted replies in 40 minutes, each sharper than the last, after Anatole receives a charged email. What should he infer first?
choices: Pause-before-send signal: his body needs time before the clean boundary is visible.
Speed-proves-serious signal: the fastest email will show the clinic means the limit.
Silence-solves-it signal: avoiding the inbox will make the intake conflict fade.

questions.prompt: Brigitte gives a Green closing reminder at the equipment cage; Benoit hints twice and then snaps. Which comparison best reads the outcomes?
choices: Hinting politeness made Benoit's later anger clearer to members near the cage.
Strictness-first thinking says closing rules work best when Benoit starts with the hardest tone.
Proportional timing helped Brigitte protect the rule before frustration had to carry it.

questions.prompt: Lane says a prepared coffee bar line sounds fake because it came from a script bank. Which reply best protects the source idea?

Perfect-wording pressure means Lane should memorize the script and avoid changing it.

questions.prompt: At the marina fuel dock, Lane writes a Red consequence that the staff cannot actually carry out. What is the main problem?
choices: Soft-language worry says the consequence should sound gentler even if nobody can enforce it.

Empty-follow-through risk means the Red line has volume but no protective action behind it.

questions.prompt: Gerard has one missed pickup notice on the repair shelf and wants to cancel the order by text. Which reading of Red is sound?

questions.prompt: Zoe changes a script-bank sentence so it sounds like her voice but leaves the limit and next action intact. How should that change be judged?
choices: Personalized structure is right when the wording changes but the boundary still has its spine.

Template loyalty is right because changing words weakens every prepared script.

questions.prompt: A week of notes shows Benoit ignored 5 small irritations, then used a Red line on the sixth incident. What pattern is most visible?
choices: High-standards framing shows Benoit waited until the issue was worth real attention.
Patience-credit framing shows Benoit earned the right to make the sixth message sharp.
People-pleasing buildup shows silence loading old resentment into a current boundary.

questions.prompt: During marina training, Gerard reviews Lane's no-phone script and asks when a Green line should become Yellow. Which answer best fits the staged method?
